title: Power Display: Inconsistent triple monitor detection after Maximum Compatibility update
author: ammaarM

status.label: Waiting for the next-release retest
status.detail: A PowerToys contributor said the next Power Display build includes bug fixes and compatibility improvements, and the reporter agreed to verify the triple-monitor behavior there.

next_action.label: Await reporter retest
next_action.reason: The current thread already has a maintainer direction and no newer evidence after the reporter agreed to retry the updated build.

judgment.rationale: The only maintainer response on the live thread directs the reporter to retry the next Power Display build after compatibility fixes, and the reporter explicitly agreed. No later comment, attachment, or linked work changes that hold state.
evidence: The issue reports that a third monitor intermittently disappears after the Maximum Compatibility update and that some controls are disabled when only two displays show up.
The issue has Product-PowerDisplay, Issue-Bug, and Needs-Triage labels with no assignee or linked pull request.
Contributor moooyo said the next version contains bug fixes and compatibility improvements and asked the reporter to try it later.
The reporter replied that they would check the next version and no further public evidence was added afterward.
judgment.recommended_action: Keep the item in waiting_on_author state until the reporter confirms whether a newer build still misses the third monitor or disabled controls.

fix_assessment.rationale: The immediate triage action is a reporter retest against the promised compatibility build. Publishing a new fix plan before that confirmation would only duplicate the existing maintainer direction.

issue_context.summary: Power Display intermittently drops the third monitor in a triple-monitor setup after the Maximum Compatibility update, but the live thread is already waiting on the reporter to retry a newer build with additional compatibility fixes.
known_information: The reporter is on PowerToys v0.100.2 installed with WinGet.
Dual-monitor setups still work for the reporter; the failure appears only in a triple-monitor setup.
When only two displays are shown, some brightness, contrast, and sound controls are greyed out or unavailable.
No bug-report ZIP, screenshot, or extra comments beyond the maintainer reply and the reporter acknowledgment are present.
The issue is labeled Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, and Product-PowerDisplay, with no assignee.
inferences: The failure likely sits in Power Display monitor discovery or capability publication under maximum-compatibility mode, because both enumeration count and per-display control availability degrade together.
The thread still lacks post-fix evidence, so it is not yet possible to distinguish a main-branch fix from a remaining regression.
issue_context.analysis: The public thread already contains the decisive next step: retry the newer build after the announced Power Display compatibility work. Replacing that with a fresh request-info or design action would regress the current maintainer direction.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body, both public comments, labels, assignees, and the empty live timeline for linked work.
Inspected src/modules/powerdisplay/PowerDisplay/ViewModels/MainViewModel.Monitors.cs, where the latest maximum-compatibility flag is forwarded before each discovery pass.
Searched related Power Display discovery issues and found older single-monitor or tray-icon reports, but no other open triple-monitor report anchored to the Maximum Compatibility update.

author_wait_evidence.author: moooyo
author_wait_evidence.requested_evidence: Retest the triple-monitor detection problem on the next PowerToys release with the latest Power Display compatibility fixes.
